title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
About The Company

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.

Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. Carrington acquired that servicer and adopted ValonOS as its core platform, allowing us to focus entirely on scaling our SaaS platform.

ValonOS is now on track to power 1 in 6 U.S. mortgages across major mortgage servicers like Newrez, Carrington, and ServiceMac. Every process on the platform is structured and programmable, enabling our AI agents to perform core servicing work, like handling payments, escrow, and homeowner questions, directly within the system's controls.

We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.

About The Role

We are seeking a Senior Analytics Engineer to take ownership of our client reporting data models and pipelines. This crucial role involves managing the layer of our data models responsible for transforming raw data into reliable, structured, and performant assets for reporting, analysis, and AI initiatives. This role sits at the intersection of analytics and data engineering, ensuring data is production-grade, auditable, and easily accessible across the organization and our customers.

You will own client reporting, standardize our data modeling practices, manage the orchestration of analytical workflows, and provide hands-on analytical support for high-stakes operational business functions, including reporting and performance management.

Responsibilities


Client Reporting & Infrastructure: Scope and develop new client reports, while also maintaining and enhancing existing reporting pipelines. Collaborate with external clients and our internal client success team to effectively manage and triage inbound requests. Partner with Valon Technologies' data team to improve the underlying infrastructure for client reporting.
Data Modeling & Transformation: Design, build, and maintain the production-grade data models and analytical layers using our existing stack of BigQuery, dbt, and Airflow to ensure reliability and structure at scale.
Data Governance & Quality: Partner with engineering and product teams to define and implement data contracts and observability frameworks to guarantee data quality and auditability for a regulated environment.
Analytical Support: Write complex SQL queries, build dashboards (in tools like Hex or Looker), and conduct ad hoc analysis to empower operational leaders and provide deep root-cause insights into business performance.


Ideal Background & Qualifications


Experience: 7+ years of combined experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or a highly technical data analytics role, ideally at a technology company or financial institution (Series B–E startup experience is a plus).
Technical Stack: Expertise in SQL (required), strong proficiency in Python, and proven experience with core modern data stack tools like dbt and Airflow.
Communication: Communicate effectively with external clients, clearly synthesizing their requests, establishing realistic timelines, and proactively managing expectations, including pushing back when necessary to ensure successful outcomes.
Architecture & Quality: Deep understanding of data architecture patterns (e.g. medallion architecture) and experience implementing data quality frameworks, observability tools, or data contracts at scale.
Analytical Tools: Experience with data visualization tools (Hex, Looker, or equivalent) and proficiency in Google Sheets/Microsoft Excel.
Mindset: A strong product mindset, focusing on the usability, reliability, and developer experience of the data systems you build.
Problem-Solving: Proven ability to solve complex problems independently and build repeatable processes around novel situations.


Minimum Qualifications


Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent professional experience in Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a similar field.t professional experience in Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a similar field.


Benefits


Compensation: competitive salary and 401(k) plan
Health & well-being: we’ll invest in your physical and mental well-being with comprehensive medical, dental, & vision benefits
Grow together: Company-wide orientation for you to successfully onboard and other learning & development opportunities, including regular review cycles that feature 360-degree feedback
Generous time off: 17 days paid time off, sick days, and 11 company holidays
Baby bonding time!: 12 weeks off for both birthing and non-birthing parents - fully paid so you can focus your energy on your newest addition


Throughout the interview process, please remember that emails will only be from valon.com email addresses. We will never ask for any personally identifiable information during the interview process itself. Please reach out to talent@valon.com if you have any requests to verify the authenticity of an outreach.

Valon is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Valon makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
Thirty Madison is now part of Remedy! You can read more about the acquisition here. We are excited to join forces and continue to revolutionize healthcare accessibility!

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Analytics Engineer within our centralized data team to own a core area of our data, such as financial performance, operations, or growth and retention, from raw sources through to the metrics leadership uses to make decisions. You'll build the dbt models and semantic layer behind those metrics. You'll also act as the analytical partner to the teams that rely on them.

This is a high-ownership role on a lean team that moves fast. Requirements often start ambiguous, and you'll be expected to find the highest-value problems before they reach anyone's roadmap.

Our stack: Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran and Hex

Comp | Perks | Benefits


The base pay range for this role is $160,000-$180,000
Potential to earn equity
Robust and affordable Medical, Dental, and Vision plan options
Flexible time off policy
Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.


What you get to do every day


Own a functional data area. Be the lead analyst for a domain like finance or growth and retention, the first person stakeholders turn to for answers and insight. You'll own its models, metrics, analysis and roadmap.
Architect core data models. Design and maintain silver and gold layer models in dbt using Kimball dimensional modeling (facts and dimensions). These power segmentation, targeting, automation and analytics for your area.
Define and operationalize metrics. Turn company-wide metrics into governed, consistent definitions. Examples include retention, funnel conversion, LTV/CAC/ROAS and revenue.
Steward the semantic layer. Treat our BI tooling (Hex) as a product. Own semantic layer health, cross-team modeling standards and self-serve data products, beyond building dashboards on request.
Make the numbers trustworthy. Set standards for testing, documentation and freshness. Lead root-cause analysis on data discrepancies, then fix the underlying architecture so they don't recur.
Partner with the business. Turn ambiguous questions from Marketing, Growth, Finance and Product into clear requirements and scalable solutions. Work without dedicated PM support and use data to influence decisions.
Communicate clearly. Explain technical decisions, trade-offs and results to audiences from engineers to senior leadership. Set and manage expectations along the way.
Improve upstream data. Work with product and engineering on event taxonomy, instrumentation quality and consistency across app, web and backend.


What you bring to the role


5+ years in analytics, analytics engineering, data engineering or a closely related role.
Deep SQL in a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake. You use it to validate data quality, investigate anomalies and back your own analysis.
Production experience with dbt: modeling, testing, documentation and project structure.
Strong data modeling skills, including Kimball dimensional modeling (star schemas, slowly changing dimensions) and layered medallion architectures. You know when to break the rules.
Business and analytical judgment. You can tell which question matters and how to answer it, not just how to model it.
A track record of leading cross-team data initiatives, including gathering requirements yourself from technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Clear, confident communication with senior leadership, including pushing back and resetting expectations when needed.
Comfort with ambiguity and a fast pace. You prioritize well and ship without waiting for perfect specs.
Hustle and a bias for action. You roll up your sleeves, do what the moment needs, whether that's a quick ad-hoc pull or a weekend fire drill on a broken pipeline, and follow through until it's done.


Bonus Points


Experience supporting Marketing, Growth, Sales or Product teams, such as attribution, paid media, funnels or retention.
Experience owning a BI platform or semantic layer (Hex, Looker, dbt Semantic Layer or similar) as a product.
Experience building semantic layers and documentation designed for AI and agentic workflows.
Familiarity with product analytics instrumentation and event tracking.
Background in consumer health, subscription or e-commerce businesses.


U.S. Applicants Only

Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Remedy we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions. Contact us at recruiting@thirtymadison.com to request accommodation.

*This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your I-9 Form information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.*


Please be aware that there are fraudulent entities who are falsely claiming to be or represent Remedy in order to solicit sensitive personal information or payment. Remedy is not in any way associated with these entities or practices. The safety and integrity of those seeking employment with us is of the utmost importance and we actively work with our legal and security teams to prevent future incidents.


Remedy will never ask for sensitive information or payment when engaging with job seekers. The entities use many methods to perpetuate these scams, including but not limited to: participating in a text-only interview, using Remedy's trademarks on their correspondence, or providing you with a seemingly legitimate offer letter. If you suspect you are a victim of this scamming, we encourage you to cease further contact and report the crime to The Federal Trade Commission.

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
The brands on your kitchen shelf are run by people doing extraordinary work that nobody sees.

title: Sr Manager Analytics Engineer
description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.

Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled.

Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day.

If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

Sr. Manager Analytics Engineer, Content Data

Req - 46420

Overview And Responsibilities

Paramount Streaming is a division of Paramount that encompasses both free, paid, and premium streaming services including Paramount+ and Pluto TV.

We are the Global Content and Lifecycle Analytics team, part of the Paramount Streaming, Data & Insights Group (DIG) team.

DIG is a key connector among the Paramount Streaming verticals. The group includes experts who create and improve data systems and products. They evaluate, combine, and analyze data. They develop insights and stories from both qualitative and quantitative data. Their work helps stakeholders make decisions. It also helps them understand performance and receive business recommendations.

Role Details

In this important role, you will develop and maintain scalable data pipelines. You will build reliable core business reasoning. You will ensure high data quality standards for content metadata. This includes titles, rights, taxonomy, and catalog data that support Paramount's streaming business.

You will work closely with analysts, data engineers, content operations, programming, licensing, and product teams. Your goal is to convert basic metadata feeds and content data into reliable datasets, dashboards, and insights. These will support decision-making for Paramount+, Pluto TV, and other Paramount streaming services.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of engineering and analytics and wants to drive data excellence at scale. This role has people management responsibilities.

Responsibilities

Pipeline Ownership: Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines. These pipelines will manage content metadata like titles, rights and licensing windows, genres, talent, franchise or series hierarchies, and availability. You will work with data engineering and analytics teams. Content Metadata Modeling: Develop and improve reliable data models. These models will unify content metadata from different sources. This includes ingest, catalog management, licensing, and rights management systems. They will support detailed reporting. This reporting will be at the title, franchise, and window levels.

Data Quality: Collaborate with software and data engineering teams. Make sure the metadata is complete, precise, and consistent. This involves identifying issues such as duplicate titles, missing or conflicting rights windows, incorrect genre or talent tagging, and misclassified territories.

Performance Monitoring: Contribute to anomaly detection systems and operational dashboards that track content catalog health, metadata completeness, and data quality KPIs. Collaboration across functions is important. You will work closely with analysts. Collaborate with content operations, programming teams, licensing, and product managers. You will translate business needs into technical data solutions. Tooling & Enablement: Build scalable, performant datasets in platforms such as Databricks, Looker, and Snowflake to enable self-service analytics for content stakeholders. Documentation & Standards: Lead the creation and maintenance of clear technical documents. Set coding standards and practices for data governance. Focus on metadata taxonomy standards and ensure compliance with content rights.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in economics, Statistics, Analytics, Computer Science, MIS, Data Engineering, or related field. 7+ years of experience in analytical engineering, data engineering, or data analytics with solid SQL and data modeling expertise.

Deep knowledge of ETL/ELT principles, data architecture, and performance optimization. Proven experience building scalable data products and pipelines using tools such as Databricks, Airflow, Spark, or similar platforms. You should have direct experience with modeling and maintaining content metadata pipelines. This includes working with title catalogs, rights and windowing data. You should also be acquainted with genre and talent taxonomies, or similar structured data in entertainment or media. Proficient ability to collaborate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders to deliver high-impact data solutions.

Fluency in building and maintaining production-grade datasets in cloud-based data environments (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery). Proficiency with BI tools such as Looker and Tableau, including building curated data layers and performance tuning. Solid data hygiene practices, including version control, code reviews, unit testing, and documentation. Exemplary problem-solving skills and attention to detail, especially when reconciling metadata inconsistencies across systems.

Additional Qualifications

Experience working with content rights and licensing data, including availability windows, territory restrictions, and content lifecycle management. Knowledge with content taxonomy and classification systems used in entertainment or media. Proficiency in Python or another scripting language for data transformation or orchestration.

Knowledge with streaming media or direct-to-consumer digital products.

Experience implementing anomaly detection systems or contributing to root cause investigations for metadata issues. Knowledge of data governance and compliance best practices as they relate to licensed content.

About Skydance

Skydance is a next-generation global media and entertainment company, comprised of three business segments: Studios, Direct-to-Consumer, and TV Media. Skydance's portfolio unites legendary brands, including Paramount, Warner Bros., HBO and HBO Max, Paramount+, Pluto TV, CBS, CNN, CBS Sports, TNT Sports, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, MTV, Food Network, BET, HGTV, and Comedy Central.

Responsibilities

description:
About Minerva

Minerva builds AI for marketing leaders. We work together with marketers to automate and accelerate their workflows with AI agents. Our agents augment the end-to-end workflow of the marketer by automating analysis, campaign planning, activation, measurement and reporting.

Our team brings together operators and investors from Citadel, Dentsu, Bridgewater, Meta Superintelligence, Growthloop, Amazon and Lazard, alongside engineers and researchers from Berkeley, MIT, Stanford and Cambridge.

THE ROLE

A warehouse full of consumer data does nothing for a marketer until they can sort, filter and chart it in the time it takes to ask the question.

Our data team builds the consumer graph and each brand's first-party models, and our data scientists train scores on top. This seat makes all of it usable in the product: first-party fields that respond instantly, scores on the pages marketers already use, segments that stay current, and an agent that turns a plain-English question into the right query against a brand's own data.

This is an IC or senior IC seat on product engineering, working day to day with data engineering and data science. Your counterpart on the warehouse side is our Staff Data Engineer, who owns the golden model and publishes the semantic views you build on.

What You'll Do


Own how first-party data performs in the app. Any field a brand connects can be sorted, filtered and charted without a live warehouse query. You decide what gets precomputed, where it lives and how it stays fresh.
Own how our models reach marketers. Propensity, LTV, churn and product-fit scores on the person, segment and product pages, with full distributions instead of a single number.
Own dynamic segments. Segments that update as new data lands, with stats ready for activation.
Own the in-app agent's query tool, built on the semantic views our data platform team publishes. You own the path from a marketer's question to the right rows.
Own the product side of the sync. What gets precomputed, and the path from Postgres to the synced client. Each hop costs money and time, and you choose on purpose.
Extend the pipelines. You mostly build on what the data team produces. When a feature needs a table that doesn't exist, you write the model or pipeline step yourself.
Ship end to end. One feature can mean a Python Lambda, a Zero schema change and a TanStack Start page. You ship all three.


OUR STACK


App: TypeScript, TanStack Start, React 19, Tailwind and Base UI, on Vite and Bun.
Sync: Zero on Postgres, schema in Drizzle. The app reads from a live-synced local copy of the data instead of request-response endpoints.
AI: Mastra for agents, Temporal for long-running work.
Backend: Python on AWS Lambda.
Data: Snowflake, including semantic views and Cortex.


WHAT YOU HAVE


Production experience with a cloud data warehouse. Snowflake preferred.
Production TypeScript, and backend services shipped on AWS: Lambda or similar.
You're current. You know what shipped in AI tooling this month and what changed in the latest release of the packages you depend on.
You build things on your own time, and you can show us.
You're in New York City or willing to relocate.


YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU ARE…


A full-stack engineer at a data-heavy SaaS company who ended up owning the warehouse because someone had to, and liked it.
A product engineer at a warehouse-native analytics or activation company who has spent years making Snowflake feel fast inside an app.
A backend engineer who has shipped on a sync engine like Zero, Replicache or ElectricSQL, and wants a dataset big enough to stress it. We'd be especially impressed by this one.
A data engineer tired of handing tables to other teams who wants to own the feature the table ends up in.
Or you don't fit any of these neatly, but you built something this year that changed how you think data should reach a user. Apply.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE


First 90 days: new scores and first-party tables reach the app through a repeatable system you built.
First 6 months: any first-party field can be sorted, filtered and charted without a live warehouse query, and the in-app agent's query tool runs on your layer.
No single number. When product engineering has a data question, it comes to you.


COMPENSATION

$170,000–$236,000 base salary, depending on level. Meaningful equity. Medical, dental and vision.

Skip the cover letter. The application asks for a demo of something you built that's relevant to what we do at Minerva: a link, a repo or a two-minute video. Applications without a demo won't be reviewed.

WHERE WE WORK

We work in person from our office at 300 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

Benefits

Every full-time role includes equity; medical, dental and vision coverage; unlimited PTO; a monthly fitness stipend; and an annual company offsite. We'd rather pay people well than buy perks nobody uses.

PAY TRANSPARENCY

The salary range in this posting is our good-faith range for the role in New York City at the time of posting. Where an offer lands depends on the level and experience we see in the interview process.

APPLYING

Apply on this page. We don't take applications by email, and we don't accept unsolicited submissions from recruiting agencies. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, write to hiring@minerva.io.

WORK AUTHORIZATION

You'll need to be authorized to work in the United States. We consider visa sponsorship case by case, so tell us on the application if you'll need it.

title: Research Analyst
description:
About Us

The Cancer Research Institute (CRI), established in 1953 and headquartered in New York City, is the preeminent U.S. nonprofit organization dedicated to saving more lives by fueling the discovery and development of powerful immunotherapies for all cancers.

Guided by a world-renowned Scientific Advisory Council that includes four Nobel laureates and 35 members of the National Academy of Sciences, CRI has invested over $517 million in support of research conducted by immunologists and tumor immunologists at the world's leading medical centers and universities and has contributed to many of the key scientific advances that demonstrate the potential for immunotherapy to change the face of cancer treatment. The Cancer Research Institute's research funding supports the entire continuum of basic discovery through early-stage clinical development of novel cancer immunotherapies.

Role

The Research Analyst will work closely with the Director of Program Operations to support analytical projects that help the Cancer Research Institute (CRI) understand and communicate the results of its research funding.

The Analyst will organize and analyze grant and research data, investigate the outputs and outcomes of CRI-funded work, and help develop reliable metrics and evidence of CRI’s impact. This work will draw on information from SmartSimple, progress reports, publications, surveys, and external research databases.

The ideal candidate is analytical, intellectually curious, familiar with the biological sciences—ideally immunology—and comfortable turning complex research information into clear, useful insights.

Responsibilities

Outcomes and Impact Tracking


Review reports, publications, surveys, and external sources to identify outcomes associated with CRI-funded research.
Track outcomes such as publications, follow-on funding, collaborations, clinical trials, intellectual property, new technologies, and investigator career progression.
Working in close partnership with Scientific Affairs, trace reported outcomes to primary sources, document the evidence behind impact claims, and assess attribution.
Assist in developing impact statements and case studies that assess the extent to whichCRI funding contributed to scientific, clinical, or career outcomes.


Research Portfolio Analysis


Support analyses of CRI funding across programs, research areas, cancer types, institutions, investigators, geography, and other relevant dimensions.
Investigate defined portfolio questions and identify trends, outliers, and data gaps.
Prepare recurring portfolio reports and ad hoc analyses.
Deliver analytical insights on grant outcomes, research trends, and portfolio metrics to Scientific Affairs and cross-functional teams to guide strategy and communications.


Data Management and Enhancement


Clean, standardize, and enhance grant, investigator, institution, publication, and research outcome data.
Identify and investigate missing, duplicate, inconsistent, or outdated information.
Apply established classifications, definitions, and validation rules maintained jointly with Scientific Affairs.
Connect information across grant records, reports, surveys, publications, and external datasets.
Document data sources and methods to support reliable and reproducible analysis.


Reporting and Analytical Tools


Prepare datasets, metrics, dashboards, visualizations, and analytical summaries.
Validate reporting data for accuracy and consistency.
